notes: All 18 assertions pass in both configurations (100% pass rate) — the current assertions do NOT discriminate between with-skill and without-skill. Claude's base knowledge of Angular routing (withPreloading, RedirectCommand, pathMatch, withComponentInputBinding, NavigationSkipped, view-transition-name) is strong enough to pass all assertions without the skill.

With-skill runs are ~66% slower (86.7s vs 52.2s mean) and use ~96% more tokens (28.5k vs 14.6k mean) due to reading multiple reference files. The skill adds overhead without improving pass rate on these assertions.

The with-skill eval 1 run used 23 tool calls (browsed router type definitions in node_modules) — this exploratory behavior suggests the skill's loading-strategies.md and route-guards.md lack the specific APIs (withPreloading, RedirectCommand) needed, forcing the agent to research them independently.

Qualitative difference: with-skill responses tend to cite skill references and cross-reference other sections (e.g., data-resolvers.md for withComponentInputBinding). Without-skill responses are more concise and self-contained.

To make these evals discriminating, assertions would need to target nuanced details that base knowledge gets wrong — for example, the binding priority order (path > query > resolve), or the fact that RedirectCommand accepts NavigationBehaviorOptions. But both configurations covered these details.
